evidence_quotes.quote: Objective: Explaining theoretically the conditions that lead to political interference in the regulatory process within a context of price regulation, for a region that has not yet achieved service universalization.
Hipótese 1 Em anos eleitorais, o grau de interferência dos políticos (σ) é mais alto sobre a atividade das agências reguladoras. Como resultado, as tarifas praticadas diminuem, em termos reais.

Com o objetivo de testar algumas das predições que podem ser obtidas do modelo, foi construída uma base de dados contendo informações sobre os reajustes anuais aplicados no Brasil no setor de saneamento (para os serviços de água, esgoto ou ambos) entre 2002 e 2021.
O vetor eleições corresponde às variáveis dummy eleições estaduaisit e eleições municipaisit para cada município (i) e período (t).
Conclusions: The findings indicate that municipal election cycles are negatively associated with prices set by regulators.

criterion_notes.c1: Topically examines the municipal water supply and sanitation sector in Brazil, modeling network expansion toward universalization theoretically (Section 3) and including municipal water and sewage population coverage rates from SNIS (Taxa_de_cobertura água and esgoto) in the empirical dataset (Section 4), although empirically coverage enters only as an explanatory variable rather than an outcome.
criterion_notes.c2: PASSES plain wording of Criterion 2, FAILS narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading. Under the plain broad wording ('legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory or governance factor'), the paper qualifies because it studies political interference and electoral cycles in subnational sanitation regulatory agencies' price-setting decisions (while also controlling for contract revisions, the 2020 Novo Marco do Saneamento, agency jurisdiction, and state vs. private utility ownership). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 clarification, however, Criterion 2 is NOT satisfied: the empirical exposure of interest is municipal and state election years (macro-political electoral cycles affecting regulator tariff adjustments), rather than a rule-type legal/administrative mechanism directly governing household or community service access, and the theoretical analysis of price-cap/Ramsey tariff rules and expansion in Section 3 is non-empirical. Even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the overall decision remains 'exclude' (plain_criterion2_decision = 'exclude') because the paper fails Criterion 4 (no empirical access or household affordability outcome).
criterion_notes.c3: Contains an empirical econometric panel-data analysis in Section 4 (983 municipality-year observations across subnational sanitation regulatory agencies in Brazil, 2002-2021). However, empirical testing is restricted exclusively to regulatory real tariff adjustments (Hypothesis 1); the analysis of network expansion (n2) and welfare in Section 3 is purely mathematical/theoretical with no empirical test.
criterion_notes.c4: No empirical outcome relevant to service access, connection, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, household affordability, or exclusion is reported. The sole dependent variable in the empirical analysis (Section 4, Tables 2 and 3) is Variação_real (annual real percentage tariff adjustment approved by regulatory agencies, nominal adjustment discounted by IPCA), framed as maintaining utility investment capacity. Municipal water and sewage coverage rates (atend_agua, atend_esgoto) are right-hand-side explanatory variables predicting tariff adjustments, and system expansion (n2) is analyzed solely in the theoretical model (Section 3).
criterion_notes.c5: Unit of analysis and sample (unbalanced municipality-year panel of regulated water/sanitation providers under 88 Brazilian subnational regulatory agencies, 2002-2021; N = 1,142 in descriptive statistics, N = 983 in regressions), exposure (municipal and state election-year dummies), empirical outcome (real regulatory tariff adjustment Variação_real), and study design (stylized two-period regulatory model plus panel-data pooled OLS, fixed effects, and random effects regressions) are identifiable.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Portuguese (with structured abstracts in Portuguese and English), which is eligible without translation under Criterion 9.

study_design: Two-period stylized microeconomic theoretical model combined with an observational unbalanced panel-data econometric study (pooled OLS, fixed effects, and random effects, 2002-2021)
population_and_sample: Brazilian municipalities with regulated water and/or sewage utilities overseen by 88 subnational sanitation regulatory agencies (46 municipal, 26 state, 16 intermunicipal) between 2002 and 2021; N = 1,142 observations in descriptive statistics (Table 1) and N = 983 municipality-year observations in panel regressions (Table 3)
exposure: Municipal and state election years (eleicoes_municipais and eleicoes_estaduais dummies capturing electoral-cycle political interference in regulatory agencies), alongside municipal water and sewage coverage rates (atend_agua, atend_esgoto) as predictors and unreported controls for contract revisions, post-July 2020 Novo Marco do Saneamento, state vs. mixed/private utility ownership, agency scope, municipal GDP, population, and 2020 pandemic year
outcome: Annual real percentage tariff adjustment set by subnational sanitation regulatory agencies (Variação_real / Reajuste_Real, nominal tariff adjustment discounted by IPCA inflation); network expansion (n2) and consumer welfare are derived solely in the non-empirical theoretical model (Section 3)
rationale: Excluded primarily under E04 (Wrong outcome), and also failing the narrow 2026-10-13 reading of Criterion 2. Although the title refers to effects of political interference in the sanitation sector on welfare and expansion of the system, full-text review shows that system expansion (n2) and welfare are modeled exclusively in a stylized two-period microeconomic theoretical model (Section 3) with no empirical testing. In the empirical panel-data econometric analysis (Section 4, Tables 2-3, N = 983 municipality-year observations, 2002-2021), the sole dependent variable is Variação_real, the annual real percentage tariff adjustment authorized by subnational regulatory agencies (nominal adjustment minus IPCA), while municipal water and sewage coverage rates (atend_agua, atend_esgoto) enter only as right-hand-side explanatory variables. Thus, no empirical household or community service access, connection, availability, continuity, quantity, household affordability, or exclusion outcome is reported (c4 = no). Additionally, under the narrow 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 scope, the empirical exposure tested is municipal and state election years (macro-political electoral cycles) rather than a rule-type legal or administrative mechanism directly governing service access (c2 = no; under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2, the study passes c2 as a regulatory/governance study of political interference in regulatory agencies, but plain_criterion2_decision remains 'exclude' due to failing Criterion 4).
